inspiration: Turn order is a sorted action queue. Order key first, then priority, then speed, and only an exact tie is broken by a random insertion point (sim/battle-queue.ts lines 18-20 and 396-401; sim/battle.ts lines 408-414). For a server tick, the same shape gives a fixed step with a seeded tie break instead of list position.

Modifiers stack as a chain of fixed-point multipliers: each multiplier is turned into a 4096ths integer, multiplied with the running value, then rounded once with a half-step offset before shifting back (sim/battle.ts lines 2318-2334). This keeps long stacks of stat modifiers from drifting and is a clean model for a stat-modifier stack in a fast duel.

Damage has a small random band, a percentage from 85 to 100 (sim/battle.ts lines 2395-2397). In the damage path it runs after the crit step and before type and STAB effects (sim/battle-actions.ts lines 1741-1742). The useful part is the order of operations, not the numbers.

The RNG is seeded and can replay a battle from seed plus decisions (sim/prng.ts lines 5-10). That is the shape of Frankendom's fight record: store the seed and the inputs, then the same duel can be replayed.

Rule variants are folders that override base tables, one folder per variant (data/mods/, 47 folders; data/mods/gen1/README.md). The shape maps to zones as data on one runtime: a zone is an overlay, not a fork.

Text has hard length budgets so a line fits its row: about 55 Latin characters for a move's short description, about 85 for an item or ability (data/text/README.md lines 21 and 25-27). This is a good budget rule for a 375 px wide HUD line.
A missing translation is written as null and falls back to English (data/text/README.md line 32). Use the same layering for any text the HUD or combat log shows.

Battle lines are templates with bracket placeholders such as the Pokemon, move and item (data/text/README.md line 38). A combat log written as templates can be restyled per language without touching the logic.

briefs.label: Duel action queue with a seeded tie break
briefs.why: Simultaneous actions resolve by a clear rule, so a faster attacker goes first and nobody wins by list position. Feels fair and is easy to read in replay.
briefs.keep: order key first, then priority, then speed; a random tie break only on exact ties
briefs.change: use the server tick's seeded RNG instead of a shared list shuffle; key the tie to character latency bucket; show the tie as a small visible tell in the replay, not hidden
briefs.ref: sim/battle-queue.ts lines 18-20 and 396-401; sim/battle.ts lines 408-414. Recreate as an original server-tick ordering; do not copy the code.

briefs.label: Fixed-point modifier stack
briefs.why: Several buffs and debuffs stack without a float drift and always resolve the same way on every machine. The stack reads as a list of named steps.
briefs.keep: each multiplier converted to an integer in fixed units; one rounding per step with a half-step offset; order fixed by event
briefs.change: use a 1000ths scale and name each stack by the buff it came from; cap the stack length at three entries for the 375 px readout; store the stack as zone data
briefs.ref: sim/battle.ts lines 2318-2334. Recreate as a distinct original stat-stack module; do not copy.

briefs.label: Damage roll band after crit
briefs.why: A narrow damage band keeps hits feeling different without making duels random. Applying it after crit and before type matters keeps the roll readable.
briefs.keep: narrow percentage band; applied after crit and before type bonus; integer rounding each step
briefs.change: use a band of our own width per weapon class; show the band as a faint number bar on the hit impact, not as a hidden roll; keep heavy hits at a tighter band
briefs.ref: sim/battle.ts lines 2395-2397; sim/battle-actions.ts lines 1741-1742. Recreate as an original hit-roll; do not copy.

briefs.label: Replay from seed and input log
briefs.why: A fight can be replayed exactly from one seed and the list of player decisions. Good for a fight record and for bug reports.
briefs.keep: one seed; log of decisions; replay gives the same result
briefs.change: store the log as a binary blob with a version byte; add a short human label per decision for the replay viewer; add a checksum at the end
briefs.ref: sim/prng.ts lines 5-10. Recreate as the Frankendom fight record; do not copy the format.

briefs.label: Type matchup as a compact grid
briefs.why: A single grid of attacker against defender type gives a readable matchup at a glance and needs no text on the screen.
briefs.keep: one table keyed by defending type, one value per attacking type (damageTaken); a small set of effect levels
briefs.change: use our own element names and palette; show each cell as a ring that gets thicker for stronger effect, not a number; keep it data-driven
briefs.ref: data/typechart.ts lines 1-4 (schema only, not copied). Recreate as an original element chart; do not copy the table.
